rules.text: The tribune of the plebs is sacrosanct and inviolable, protected by oaths sworn by plebeians.
The tribune of the plebs has the power to veto any political act (intercessio) and to protect any individual from injustice committed by a magistrate (auxilium).
Plebiscites, decrees of the concilium plebis, have the force of law for all Romans following the lex Hortensia of 287 BC.
The senate has the power to declare a law invalid under the lex Caecilia Didia.
The comitia centuriata is the only assembly where capital charges could be brought.
The censors have the power to control membership in the Senate and expel senators for bad character, criminal offense, or infamia.
The dictator holds summum imperium and supreme authority within the scope of his mandate.
The interrex is appointed when there are no curule magistrates in office and has the authority to summon the senate and assemblies.
The lex Villia annalis of 180 BC formalised the cursus honorum by setting minimum ages for each office.
The lex Gabinia tabellaria and lex Cassia tabellaria introduced the secret ballot.
The lex Domitia de sacerdotis of 104 BC abolished the cooption of priests in favour of election.
Sulla's reforms required that all bills presented to the assemblies first be approved by the senate.
Sulla's reforms restricted the tribunician veto to only matters of individual requests for clemency.
Sulla's reforms required that men elected tribune would be barred from all other magistracies.
The lex Titia of 43 BC created the trimvirate, devolving the people's powers of election, appeal, and legislation to the triumvirs.

ministries.name: Assemblies
ministries.mandate: Served as the supreme repository of political power with authority to elect magistrates, accept or reject laws, administer justice, and declare war or peace.

ministries.name: Senate
ministries.mandate: Advised the magistrates, resolved disputes between magistrates, and oversaw the allocation of public resources and responsibilities.
ministries.veto_scope: A motion could be vetoed by a consul or one of the plebeian tribunes; the senate had power to declare a law invalid under lex Caecilia Didia.

ministries.name: Consuls
ministries.mandate: Supreme magistrates for an annual term endowed with imperium to command in civic and military spheres.
ministries.veto_scope: Each magistrate could veto one of their colleagues; a motion in the senate could be vetoed by a consul.

ministries.name: Praetors
ministries.mandate: Administered justice, commanded military forces, and governed provinces.
ministries.veto_scope: Each magistrate could veto one of their colleagues.

ministries.name: Censors
ministries.mandate: Conducted the census, controlled membership in the Senate, and were responsible for public morality.

ministries.name: Plebeian tribunes
ministries.mandate: Protected the rights of plebeians and could veto political acts or protect individuals from injustice.
ministries.veto_scope: Could veto any political act (intercessio) and protect any individual from injustice (auxilium); could veto a motion in the senate.

ministries.name: Aediles
ministries.mandate: In charge of municipal tasks such as upkeep of temples, streets, water-supply, and public games.

ministries.name: Quaestors
ministries.mandate: Elected administrators in charge of the treasury, granaries, or administrative postings.

ministries.name: Dictator
ministries.mandate: Extraordinary magistrate with summum imperium and supreme authority within the scope of his mandate.

ministries.name: Magister equitum
ministries.mandate: Lieutenant to the dictator with similar plenary authority.

ministries.name: Interrex
ministries.mandate: Extraordinary magistrate appointed when there were no curule magistrates in office to hold elections.
